turn_text: Welcome to Growth Without Barriers, the podcast of the Small Business and Entrepreneurship Council at sbecounsel.org.

I'm here with Senator Marco Rubio from Florida. He's also Chairman of the Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship. And we are going to talk about the stimulus package, in particular the Paycheck Protection Program. Senator, welcome. Thank you for joining us.
Thank you. I appreciate you having me on.

So this entire stimulus package obviously is a big deal, a very big deal. And let's focus this conversation today on the Paycheck Protection Program. What do you want small business owners and entrepreneurs to know about it?

That it's an effort to make sure that we have a small business backbone to our economy that remains in place once we clear through this. Look, I think all businesses big and small are being challenged right now. in ways that they've never been challenged before. We're basically operating in a country that for the public health reasons, we're telling people that they can't open their doors and we're telling customers they can't go visit you and spend money with you. So it's a very unusual situation. This is not an economic downturn and this is not about helping companies that were failing. These are very successful companies, some of which were having the best years ever and were thriving. And from one moment to the next, the bottom fell out. The program was designed to be simple, simple as possible. I approach what I'm about to say with some humility. This is not something that's ever been done before. So we think it can work. We had a very limited period of time to put it together. And so what I'd like to do is just sort of describe the program and its most basic terms. And then obviously there's greater level of detail, but so this applies. who's eligible is any business that either meets the SBA criteria for small business or has 500 employees or less, as well as not-for-profits 501c3s and independent contractors, so kid economy, people that work for themselves, self-employed, and so forth. What they are eligible for is 250% of their monthly payroll as it existed before the crisis hit. And the way you get it, and you get this money, And if you use it for payroll for rent or lease or utility payments or benefits for your employer or a combination of all of that, as long as you spend it on that, you don't have to pay it back. And the way you would get it is not through a government office, you would go to a lender. I think ideally if it's a small business that has an existing banking relationship Through them, most of not all the banks in this country are going to participate in this program. And the lender would verify that you're a business. If it's a preexisting banking relationship, that's going to be easy. They've already done that. They're going to verify your payroll with the payroll amount and therefore what your eligibility amount is. And they're going to transfer the money. And they're finalizing all the details on it now, but we anticipate it's going to be a quick process or one or two page application that can be done online. And again, no collateral, no credit check. And it really isn't alone unless you spend all or portions of that money on uses outside of payroll, benefits, rent or lease and utilities. If you spend any portion of that in that way, then a year from now, it turns into a low interest SBA loan.
